tasks.task: Follow-up to the earlier fog fix (task 104, already fixed: density=0 no longer renders black, brightness no longer inverts with density). tasks.title: Recompile scripts in place
tasks.task:
Editing a script in the Script Editor recompiles it on every change. compile() currently does types_[name] = std::move(newClassInfo), which frees the old ClassInfo while the component-registry factory lambda and every already-attached ScriptComponent still point at it -> use-after-free / crash when the script is then added to an actor or Play is pressed.

Fix: recompile IN PLACE. Keep the same ClassInfo object (stable pointer); swap its decl, re-resolve the base, re-index functions. Live ScriptObjects whose class changed should drop their cached state so field initialisers re-run and do_async resume indices reset.

tasks.title: Script editor: accepting autocomplete with Tab/Enter inserts a stray tab/newline first
tasks.task:
Reported while testing the new Fog component: open the script editor, get an autocomplete popup open (type any identifier prefix that matches something), then press Tab (or Enter) to accept. Instead of just inserting the completion, a literal tab character (looked like an extra space) gets inserted right before the completion text, corrupting the line ('messing up the autocomplete completely').

Root cause: ScriptEditor::updateAutocomplete()'s per-frame character-forwarding loop (which forwards typed characters to keep the word growing while the popup is open, since TextEditor's own keyboard handling is disabled in that state) reads every character in io.InputQueueCharacters -- including '\t'/'\r'/'\n', which land there too when Tab/Enter is pressed, not just via ImGui::IsKeyPressed(). Those aren't alnum/underscore, so they fall into the loop's generic 'insert whatever this is' branch and get inserted as literal characters, immediately followed by the separate 'if (accept) { insert completion suffix }' block also firing for the same keypress -- so you get tab-then-completion instead of just the completion.

Fix applied on the rendering branch (2026-09-15): skip '\t'/'\r'/'\n' entirely in that forwarding loop (continue, no insert, don't touch acOpen_) since Tab/Enter acceptance is handled separately right below. User confirmed live ('seems to be fixed').

Note: the scripting branch's ScriptEditor.cpp has the identical loop structure (handleBracketCharForAc's else-branch has the same gap) and very likely has the same bug -- worth porting this same one-line-per-branch fix over there next time that branch is touched.

requirements.text: autocomplete accept via Tab inserts only the completion, no stray tab/newline

tasks.title: variables
tasks.task:
here we will setup base system types used for all or most components, as well as some of the data they will use.

note, the syntax for a base class is uppercase first letter. 'ie Actor" returns the global type actor, its what you should set your variable as to use a Actor reference. Lowercase is for instance 'ie actor" which returns the actor. for instance.

Actor a = this.actor; would return the actor base of the type.

if the object has a component that inherits from actor you can get it with this.get_component(type_of(Actor)); which returns the actor (or whatever type you give it). Or
Actor a = this.actor;
Actor b = a.get_component(type_of(Actor));

in that case get_component is a function of Actor, which a is an instance of. type_of is a global function which is used to pass a type.

Arrays can take any type even in the same array, and can be accessed via array_name[index] which returns it.

tasks.title: Live component reload and registry cleanup
tasks.task:
Two loose ends from live editing:
1. Renaming a class inside a script leaves the old name in the Add Component menu forever (ComponentRegistry::add dedupes by name and never replaces / removes).
2. A ScriptComponent already on an actor keeps running the old code until it is removed and re-added.

Fix: when a class is renamed, drop the old registry entry (or rename it); when a class recompiles, invalidate the cached ScriptObject on every attached ScriptComponent so edits take effect in the same session.

tasks.title: Found and fixed the root cause of the Asset Browser click-blocking bug
tasks.task:
The user reported 'still cant click anyhting in the asset browser' while I was mid-investigation on item 15 (asset drag-to-folder). Reproduced live: single clicks, double-clicks, and drags on every Asset Browser tile were all silently swallowed.

ROOT CAUSE: Step 2's prefab-extraction drop target (an ImGui::InvisibleButton spanning the whole 'files' child window, added so a Hierarchy actor could be dragged onto the Asset Browser to extract a prefab) was submitted before every asset tile in that same child, without ImGui::SetNextItemAllowOverlap(). Dear ImGui's ActiveId is claimed on mouse-DOWN by whichever item is hovered at that instant -- since the invisible button was submitted first, it always won that race, even though the real tiles are drawn visually on top of it afterward. Every tile drawn inside that child was effectively dead to mouse input from the moment Step 2 shipped. This is almost certainly the real cause behind several separate-looking user reports: the Asset Browser going fully unresponsive, .cscene files not being draggable (item 105), and item 15's drag-to-folder never registering.

FIX: one ImGui::SetNextItemAllowOverlap() call before the InvisibleButton (EditorApp.cpp, drawBottomPanel). Rebuilt, killed the stale locked exe, relaunched, and re-verified live: folder single-click/double-click/navigation, script and image tile selection, and the CRATE_ASSET_MOVE drag (item 15/15b) all work correctly now -- confirmed by screenshot at every step, including moving Default.inputmap into assets/scripts/ and back out again.

ALSO SHIPPED (same commit): scenes can now be dragged directly from the Asset Browser onto a Hierarchy row (instantiates as that actor's child) or onto empty Hierarchy space (instantiates at the scene root) -- the user asked for this mid-session after confirming the existing viewport-drop instantiate flow worked. Verified live both ways.

Full 28-target test suite passes (0 failures). Both Debug (build/) and Release (build-Release/) rebuilt.

customValues.77f8b466f2874429a253d2256f62c42a: currently we have a hard coded startup scene, now we are going to create scenes (like in godot, or levels / prefabs in unity) A scene is a collection of Actors. Scenes are saved in the asset browser and can be instantiated. a New scene can be made via the new scene toolbar button, right click -> new scene in the asset menu, or file->new scene in the top tool bar. Multiple scenes can be open in the scene view via a tabbed interface. double clicking a scene asset opens it. When the game starts a blank scene is created called root. this scene can be gotten by calling get_root() which returns a Scene of type Actor. Scenes can be nested within other scenes. Draging a scene to the asset window creates a new saved scene (after prompting for a name) and it then contains the scene you dragged and ALL of its children. The scene tree scene is then deleted, and replaced with the new prefab. The children of the scene you made an asset will not be visible unless you open the scene. Scene prefabs are blue in color. Scenes are of type Asset for reference assignment. If a script wants an Asset type that means with wants a Saved Scene file. If it wants an actor then it wants a Actor from the scene tree or a instantiated scene.

Scenes/Projects kickoff plan (2026-09-16).

Both tasks moved here from main at the user's request. Git branch project-management created off main (which already includes the two commits from the session-handoff note above) for this work. Builds for this branch go to a separate  uild-scenes/ CMake build directory so they never overwrite  uild/ or  uild-Release/Crate.exe -- the user is actively testing the current build while this branch's work proceeds. Per explicit instruction, zen.tasks.json's latestExePath/latestReleasePath were left untouched.

Scenes is the larger and more foundational of the two tasks -- starting there, Projects after. Current engine state (confirmed by direct code search before starting): Scene/Scene.cpp has ZERO serialization today. EditorApp::EditorApp() hardcodes Scene::makeSample() and File > Save is a stub that only logs "Scene serialization arrives with the Data branch." Everything in the Scenes task spec (asset-browser scene tiles, tabbed multi-scene view, the root scene / get_root(), nested scenes, drag-to-asset-window prefab extraction, blue prefab coloring, Asset-vs-Actor reference typing) depends on real Scene (de)serialization existing first.

Planned incremental approach (this is a large task, likely spans multiple sessions the way Transplation did):
1. Scene serialization format + Scene::save()/Scene::load() covering the actor hierarchy, transforms, and every existing component type's fields (mesh renderer, light, camera, fog, volumetric fog, light probe, spinner, script components including field values).
2. Asset Browser integration: scene files as a recognized asset type, new-scene creation (toolbar button / right-click in asset menu / File > New Scene), double-click to open.
3. Root scene concept + get_root() script API (a blank "root" scene created when the game starts).
4. Tabbed multi-scene Scene View (multiple open scenes at once).
5. Prefab/nested-scene instancing: drag-to-asset-window extraction workflow, blue prefab coloring, Asset-type vs Actor-type distinction for script reference fields.

Will post further notes here as milestones land. Progress commits happen on the project-management branch only; nothing here touches main or the build the user is testing.

tasks.title: Scenes Phase 1 done: Scene::save()/load() serialization
tasks.task:
Scenes Phase 1 complete and committed (2026-09-16, commit efc14b4 on project-management).

Implemented full Scene::save()/Scene::load() serialization -- the foundational piece the rest of the Scenes task spec depends on. Summary:
- New hand-rolled text format (documented in full at the top of src/scene/SceneIO.cpp): actor hierarchy, transforms, visible/enabled flags, and every component's fields.
- Component and Actor both gained writeFields()/readField() virtuals, implemented for all 7 builtin components (MeshRenderer, Light, Fog, Volumetric Fog, Camera, Light Probe, Spinner) and SpriteActor/UIControlActor's extra fields.
